data.exact_reserve_text: Included within net claims incurred of GBP 68.6m (2014: GBP 57.7m) is a release of GBP 1.2m from claims reserves established at the prior year.

The 2014 year of account has a forecast return in the range of 4% to 9% on stamp capacity at the 24 month stage. Whilst the year has benefited from a relatively low level of catastrophe events, the result has absorbed losses from Hurricane Odile and two notable risk losses on the Energy account.

The 2014 year of account has a forecast return in the range of 4% to 9% on stamp capacity at the 24 month stage. Whilst the year has benefited from a relatively low level of catastrophe events, the result has absorbed losses from Hurricane Odile and two notable risk losses on the Energy account.

The account performed better than plan gross of reinsurance but due to the catastrophe losses falling below the attachment of the reinsurance programme the account performed broadly in line with the original business plan net of reinsurance. We have managed to reduce the attachment point of the reinsurance programme for Mexico events for the later years of account.

The class also suffered two notable large loss events; a diamond theft and a cash in transit loss. This volatility has affected the account's performance relative to plan resulting in an underwriting loss after reinsurance.

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate reported a net release of GBP 1.2 million from claims reserves established in prior years. This release contributed to the overall financial result. The claims development triangle for prior years (2011-2013) shows no movement in ultimate claims estimates. The 2013 year of account was impacted by Hurricanes Manuel and Ingrid, Central European flooding, and the Julius Klein Diamond heist, as well as a diamond theft and cash in transit loss. The 2014 year of account absorbed losses from Hurricane Odile and two notable risk losses on the Energy account.
